title: BBC Russian reveals that journalist Darya Shipacheva raised 1.5 million rubles for Ukraine’s military before receiving a 12-year treason sentence
text: Darya Shipacheva during her sentencing at Moscow City Court, July 29, 2026 The case of medical journalist Darya Shipacheva, sentenced to 12 years in a penal colony for treason in July 2026, drew widespread attention. A photograph of her in handcuffs in the courtroom spread across social media. Her trial was held behind closed doors, and almost nothing was known about the substance of the charges. BBC Russian has learned exactly what led to her conviction. Meduza summarizes its findings. Shipacheva raised money for Ukraine’s armed forces on behalf of Ukrainian blogger Vasilisa Levchenko, BBC Russian reported. According to investigators, Shipacheva transferred more than 1.5 million rubles to Levchenko. Darya Shipacheva is 35. Before her arrest, she wrote about medicine, health, and feminism for RBC, Takie Dela , Wonderzine, and Forbes Woman . She also published a book about medicine and health, “Bez paniki” (“Don’t Panic”). As an activist, she organized demonstrations in support of the Khachaturyan sisters and feminist activist Yulia Tsvetkova . title: Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now' as US envoy to meet Putin in Russia
text: Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now' as US envoy to meet Putin in Russia Figure caption, Watch: Zelensky says US military intelligence sharing "works now" By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Ewe Koh Published 20 October 2026 Updated 21 October 2026 US special envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in Russia to meet President Vladimir Putin after Ukraine's leader said American intelligence sharing about deadly Russian strikes "works now". Kyiv had accused the US of recently withholding such intelligence, causing Ukrainians to lose their lives - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by Washington. Volodymyr Zelensky was speaking after meeting Witkoff in Oslo on Tuesday for talks later described as "constructive" by a US official. The Ukrainian president and his European allies said it was now up to Russia to respond to the proposals agreed in Oslo when Witkoff meets Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss measures to end the war. Putin is yet to publicly comment on the latest developments, but Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said the Kremlin will listen to what Witkoff offers while ruling out "any political concessions". title: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist
text: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist By AFP Oct. 21, 2026 Imai Yuki. Social media Japan sent a senior diplomat to Moscow this week to discuss the release of a journalist arrested in Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said Wednesday. Russia’s FSB security service said last week that a Japanese national had been arrested on the Far Eastern island of Sakhalin. The individual was later identified as Yuki Imai from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, who faces accusations of "conducting espionage activities on Russian territory." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has denied that Japan conducts spying activities in Russia, while the Hokkaido Shimbun has stressed its independence from the government. On Tuesday, Kimitake Nakamura, Japan's top diplomat for Europe, met Lyudmila Vorobyova, the head of the department at the Russian Foreign Ministry dealing with much of East Asia, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry. "We lodged a request... that calls for the earliest possible realization of consular access to the Japanese national detained in Russia, as well as the individual's immediate release," Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told reporters

title: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight
text: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight Oct. 21, 2026 Anna Zvereva (CC BY-SA 2.0) A Russian Su-30 fighter jet crashed in the western Kaliningrad region during a routine training flight, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday. The two-member crew successfully ejected from the aircraft and was later found by a search and rescue team, the ministry said, adding that “there is no threat to the lives of the pilots.” It added that the fighter jet crashed in an unpopulated area and was not carrying any weapons on board. The cause of the incident was not immediately clear. Some Russian news outlets reported that the Su-30 went down in an area surrounding the Chernyakhovsk naval airbase, a hub for the Russian Navy’s Baltic Sea Fleet. An eyewitness video circulating on social media showed a fireball and a thick column of smoke rising in the air following the crash. In the video, a group of men in military uniforms are seen standing at a cemetery, which is located east of the airbase, looking toward the site of the incident. text: Armenia Appeals to Eurasian Economic Union for Removal of Russian Trade Restrictions Oct. 21, 2026 Alexander Nemenov / AFP Armenia has asked the Moscow-led Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) to designate Russia’s growing trade restrictions on Armenian goods as illegal market barriers, the newspaper Kommersant reported Wednesday, citing the South Caucasus country’s economic minister. Russia has issued sweeping bans on a range of Armenian products this year as Yerevan, Moscow’s historical ally, began the process of joining the European Union. text: Solzhenitsyn Statue Temporarily Returned to Original Vladivostok Site After Relocation Mishap Oct. 21, 2026 Novosti VL / vl.ru/news Authorities in the Far Eastern port city of Vladivostok have temporarily returned a controversial monument to Nobel Prize-winning Soviet dissident Alexander Solzhenitsyn to its original location after a failed attempt to relocate it. The statue was dismantled from the waterfront promenade in central Vladivostok on Tuesday, with plans to place it in a nearby, smaller square. However, on Wednesday, the Vladivostok city hall’s press service told Interfax that workers realized the statue was too large for the smaller square when attempting to install it there. “The monument visually overloads the small recreational zone,” a press spokesperson was quoted as saying. Officials confirmed that the Solzhenitsyn monument will remain at the original Ship Embankment until architects finish modifying the Faith and Hope Square, where it was intended to be moved. text: Putin Releases American Jailed in Russia, Agrees to Trilateral Peace Talks as Witkoff Visits Oct. 21, 2026 U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff meets with Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg on Oct. 21, 2026. Kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday announced the release of Stephen James Hubbard, an American teacher who was taken from his home in Ukraine after Russia's full-scale invasion, as the Kremlin leader met with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg to discuss restarting negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. title: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist
text: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist By AFP Oct. 21, 2026 Imai Yuki. Social media Japan sent a senior diplomat to Moscow this week to discuss the release of a journalist arrested in Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said Wednesday. Russia’s FSB security service said last week that a Japanese national had been arrested on the Far Eastern island of Sakhalin. The individual was later identified as Yuki Imai from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, who faces accusations of "conducting espionage activities on Russian territory." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has denied that Japan conducts spying activities in Russia, while the Hokkaido Shimbun has stressed its independence from the government. On Tuesday, Kimitake Nakamura, Japan's top diplomat for Europe, met Lyudmila Vorobyova, the head of the department at the Russian Foreign Ministry dealing with much of East Asia, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry. "We lodged a request... that calls for the earliest possible realization of consular access to the Japanese national detained in Russia, as well as the individual's immediate release," Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told reporters

title: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight
text: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight Oct. 21, 2026 Anna Zvereva (CC BY-SA 2.0) A Russian Su-30 fighter jet crashed in the western Kaliningrad region during a routine training flight, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday. The two-member crew successfully ejected from the aircraft and was later found by a search and rescue team, the ministry said, adding that “there is no threat to the lives of the pilots.” It added that the fighter jet crashed in an unpopulated area and was not carrying any weapons on board. The cause of the incident was not immediately clear. Some Russian news outlets reported that the Su-30 went down in an area surrounding the Chernyakhovsk naval airbase, a hub for the Russian Navy’s Baltic Sea Fleet. An eyewitness video circulating on social media showed a fireball and a thick column of smoke rising in the air following the crash. In the video, a group of men in military uniforms are seen standing at a cemetery, which is located east of the airbase, looking toward the site of the incident. title: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks
text: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks Image source, Reuters Image caption, Russia has in recent weeks intensified its deadly missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 21 October 2026 Ukraine's capital has come under a new missile attack, hours after Russia said it was "ready in principle" to resume peace talks and the US president said the world was "the closest we've been" to ending the war. Several houses were hit on Wednesday night, injuring six people, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said. The attack came amid a new diplomatic push led by Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Witkoff met Russia's President Vladimir Putin in the city of St Petersburg on Wednesday - a day after meeting Ukraine's leader. Three-way talks were paused in February, after which Russia stepped up attacks as Ukraine ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles. title: Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push
text: Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Witkoff (R) said there was still important work to do after the meeting with Putin (L) By Steve Rosenberg Russia Editor ,Â Reporting from Moscow Published 21 October 2026 After two days of diplomacy â in Norway's capital and Russia's St Petersburg â is the war in Ukraine any closer to ending? "Good and constructive" is how Norway's prime minister described Tuesday's talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, US President Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and European representatives. title: Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now' as US envoy to meet Putin in Russia
text: Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now' as US envoy to meet Putin in Russia Figure caption, Watch: Zelensky says US military intelligence sharing "works now" By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Ewe Koh Published 20 October 2026 Updated 21 October 2026 US special envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in Russia to meet President Vladimir Putin after Ukraine's leader said American intelligence sharing about deadly Russian strikes "works now". Kyiv had accused the US of recently withholding such intelligence, causing Ukrainians to lose their lives - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by Washington. Volodymyr Zelensky was speaking after meeting Witkoff in Oslo on Tuesday for talks later described as "constructive" by a US official. The Ukrainian president and his European allies said it was now up to Russia to respond to the proposals agreed in Oslo when Witkoff meets Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss measures to end the war. Putin is yet to publicly comment on the latest developments, but Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said the Kremlin will listen to what Witkoff offers while ruling out "any political concessions". title: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist
text: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist By AFP Oct. 21, 2026 Imai Yuki. Social media Japan sent a senior diplomat to Moscow this week to discuss the release of a journalist arrested in Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said Wednesday. Russia’s FSB security service said last week that a Japanese national had been arrested on the Far Eastern island of Sakhalin. The individual was later identified as Yuki Imai from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, who faces accusations of "conducting espionage activities on Russian territory." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has denied that Japan conducts spying activities in Russia, while the Hokkaido Shimbun has stressed its independence from the government. On Tuesday, Kimitake Nakamura, Japan's top diplomat for Europe, met Lyudmila Vorobyova, the head of the department at the Russian Foreign Ministry dealing with much of East Asia, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry. "We lodged a request... that calls for the earliest possible realization of consular access to the Japanese national detained in Russia, as well as the individual's immediate release," Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told reporters

title: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight
text: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight Oct. 21, 2026 Anna Zvereva (CC BY-SA 2.0) A Russian Su-30 fighter jet crashed in the western Kaliningrad region during a routine training flight, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday. The two-member crew successfully ejected from the aircraft and was later found by a search and rescue team, the ministry said, adding that “there is no threat to the lives of the pilots.” It added that the fighter jet crashed in an unpopulated area and was not carrying any weapons on board. The cause of the incident was not immediately clear. Some Russian news outlets reported that the Su-30 went down in an area surrounding the Chernyakhovsk naval airbase, a hub for the Russian Navy’s Baltic Sea Fleet. An eyewitness video circulating on social media showed a fireball and a thick column of smoke rising in the air following the crash. In the video, a group of men in military uniforms are seen standing at a cemetery, which is located east of the airbase, looking toward the site of the incident. title: Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now' as US envoy to meet Putin in Russia

Kremlin.ru President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday announced the release of Stephen James Hubbard, an American teacher who was taken from his home in Ukraine after Russia's full-scale invasion, as the Kremlin leader met with U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg to discuss restarting negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. Putin told Witkoff that Hubbard, convicted in Russia on allegations of serving as a mercenary for the Ukrainian military, was already preparing to board a flight back to the United States. Washington had maintained that the 74-year-old Michigan native and former teacher was wrongfully detained and sentenced to six years in prison. U.S. President Donald Trump told reporters at the Oval Office earlier in the week that he had personally asked Putin to release Hubbard ahead of Witkoff's trip to St. Petersburg. title: FSB Arrests German Accused of Fighting for Ukraine
text: FSB Arrests German Accused of Fighting for Ukraine Oct. 21, 2026 A man, identified as a German military veteran, arrested by the Russian Federal Security Service FSB Russia’s FSB security service has arrested a German citizen accused of serving as a mercenary for the Ukrainian military before deserting his unit, Russian state media reported Wednesday. The man, who was identified only by his birth year of 1976, is reportedly a former German military veteran with a history of combat deployments in Afghanistan, Somalia and Syria. The FSB claimed the man also served as a sniper in a Ukrainian territorial defense unit between 2016 and 2018 near the Russian-occupied city of Donetsk. In a video interrogation published by the state-run TASS news agency, the German national said he had left for Switzerland after completing his contract. He said he re-entered Ukraine in November 2025 and signed a new three-year contract in December. “I was promised 100,000 hryvnias ($2,200). However, I didn’t receive the money and was forced to flee the ranks of the armed forces of Ukraine,” the man said. title: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist
text: Japan Sends Senior Diplomat to Russia to Seek Release of Arrested Journalist By AFP Oct. 21, 2026 Imai Yuki. Social media Japan sent a senior diplomat to Moscow this week to discuss the release of a journalist arrested in Russia on spying accusations, Tokyo said Wednesday. Russia’s FSB security service said last week that a Japanese national had been arrested on the Far Eastern island of Sakhalin. The individual was later identified as Yuki Imai from the Hokkaido Shimbun newspaper, who faces accusations of "conducting espionage activities on Russian territory." Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi has denied that Japan conducts spying activities in Russia, while the Hokkaido Shimbun has stressed its independence from the government. On Tuesday, Kimitake Nakamura, Japan's top diplomat for Europe, met Lyudmila Vorobyova, the head of the department at the Russian Foreign Ministry dealing with much of East Asia, according to Japan's Foreign Ministry. "We lodged a request... that calls for the earliest possible realization of consular access to the Japanese national detained in Russia, as well as the individual's immediate release," Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara told reporters

title: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight
text: Fighter Jet Crashes in Kaliningrad Region During Training Flight Oct. 21, 2026 Anna Zvereva (CC BY-SA 2.0) A Russian Su-30 fighter jet crashed in the western Kaliningrad region during a routine training flight, Russia’s Defense Ministry said Wednesday. The two-member crew successfully ejected from the aircraft and was later found by a search and rescue team, the ministry said, adding that “there is no threat to the lives of the pilots.” It added that the fighter jet crashed in an unpopulated area and was not carrying any weapons on board. The cause of the incident was not immediately clear. Some Russian news outlets reported that the Su-30 went down in an area surrounding the Chernyakhovsk naval airbase, a hub for the Russian Navy’s Baltic Sea Fleet. An eyewitness video circulating on social media showed a fireball and a thick column of smoke rising in the air following the crash. In the video, a group of men in military uniforms are seen standing at a cemetery, which is located east of the airbase, looking toward the site of the incident. title: Armenia Appeals to Eurasian Economic Union for Removal of Russian Trade Restrictions
text: Armenia Appeals to Eurasian Economic Union for Removal of Russian Trade Restrictions Oct. 21, 2026 Alexander Nemenov / AFP Armenia has asked the Moscow-led Eurasian Economic Union (EAEU) to designate Russia’s growing trade restrictions on Armenian goods as illegal market barriers, the newspaper Kommersant reported Wednesday, citing the South Caucasus country’s economic minister. Russia has issued sweeping bans on a range of Armenian products this year as Yerevan, Moscow’s historical ally, began the process of joining the European Union. Amid the mounting restrictions, the EU relaxed tariffs on around 80% of Armenian exports for the next two years. “We consider the [Russian] restrictions against us to be unlawful,” Armenian Economy Minister Gevorg Papoyan told reporters, according to the Kommersant. “If these restrictions are recognized as a barrier, then Russia is obliged to remove them within 30 days per EAEU procedures,” Papoyan was quoted as saying. He added that Armenia has already submitted individual appeals to each trade restriction introduced in recent months, and in one case, it allegedly secured the support of three other members of the economic union. title: Solzhenitsyn Statue Temporarily Returned to Original Vladivostok Site After Relocation Mishap
text: Solzhenitsyn Statue Temporarily Returned to Original Vladivostok Site After Relocation Mishap Oct. 21, 2026 Novosti VL / vl.ru/news Authorities in the Far Eastern port city of Vladivostok have temporarily returned a controversial monument to Nobel Prize-winning Soviet dissident Alexander Solzhenitsyn to its original location after a failed attempt to relocate it. The statue was dismantled from the waterfront promenade in central Vladivostok on Tuesday, with plans to place it in a nearby, smaller square. However, on Wednesday, the Vladivostok city hall’s press service told Interfax that workers realized the statue was too large for the smaller square when attempting to install it there. “The monument visually overloads the small recreational zone,” a press spokesperson was quoted as saying. Officials confirmed that the Solzhenitsyn monument will remain at the original Ship Embankment until architects finish modifying the Faith and Hope Square, where it was intended to be moved. They did not provide a timeframe. title: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks
text: Missiles hit Kyiv after Russia agrees to US call to resume Ukraine peace talks Image source, Reuters Image caption, Russia has in recent weeks intensified its deadly missile and drone attacks on Kyiv and other Ukrainian cities By Jaroslav Lukiv Published 21 October 2026 Ukraine's capital has come under a new missile attack, hours after Russia said it was "ready in principle" to resume peace talks and the US president said the world was "the closest we've been" to ending the war. Several houses were hit on Wednesday night, injuring six people, Kyiv Mayor Vitaliy Klitschko said. The attack came amid a new diplomatic push led by Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner. Witkoff met Russia's President Vladimir Putin in the city of St Petersburg on Wednesday - a day after meeting Ukraine's leader. Three-way talks were paused in February, after which Russia stepped up attacks as Ukraine ran out of Western-supplied interceptors to defend against missiles. title: Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push
text: Rosenberg: Russia agrees to Ukraine talks but sees little to talk about in new peace push Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Witkoff (R) said there was still important work to do after the meeting with Putin (L) By Steve Rosenberg Russia Editor ,Â Reporting from Moscow Published 21 October 2026 After two days of diplomacy â in Norway's capital and Russia's St Petersburg â is the war in Ukraine any closer to ending? "Good and constructive" is how Norway's prime minister described Tuesday's talks between Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, US President Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff and European representatives. title: Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now' as US envoy to meet Putin in Russia
text: Zelensky says intelligence sharing 'works now' as US envoy to meet Putin in Russia Figure caption, Watch: Zelensky says US military intelligence sharing "works now" By Jaroslav Lukiv Â and Â Ewe Koh Published 20 October 2026 Updated 21 October 2026 US special envoy Steve Witkoff has arrived in Russia to meet President Vladimir Putin after Ukraine's leader said American intelligence sharing about deadly Russian strikes "works now". Kyiv had accused the US of recently withholding such intelligence, causing Ukrainians to lose their lives - a claim rejected as "scandalous" by Washington. Volodymyr Zelensky was speaking after meeting Witkoff in Oslo on Tuesday for talks later described as "constructive" by a US official. The Ukrainian president and his European allies said it was now up to Russia to respond to the proposals agreed in Oslo when Witkoff meets Putin in St Petersburg on Wednesday to discuss measures to end the war. Putin is yet to publicly comment on the latest developments, but Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov has said the Kremlin will listen to what Witkoff offers while ruling out "any political concessions".
